selected_scope.name: in_process_persistent_resident_device_handle_storage
selected_scope.reason: the existing runner is process-scoped, so the first real persistent handle should keep one CUDA context and one device allocation alive across phases inside a single invocation before attempting cross-process persistence

storage_contract.device_storage: reuse the same d_storage allocation across all persistent phases
storage_contract.initialization: phase 1 may upload the CPU-generated 1x1 init-state once
storage_contract.phase_advancement: phases 2..N advance from the existing d_storage contents without --init-state
storage_contract.final_dump: optional per-phase dump is diagnostic and compare evidence, not the authority for the next phase
storage_contract.state_authority: GPU d_storage is authoritative after phase 1 initialization

required_behavior: when persistent handle is requested, treat ENV_PERSISTENT_RESIDENT_PHASE as the reported phase index
for the first implemented measurement, run exactly one phase per process until a multi-phase process driver is added
do not accept phase > 1 without a device-resident handle lookup
print setup and phase timing fields without changing existing resident timing lines
invoke a single persistent process or explicit future runner mode instead of chaining prior GPU dumps through --init-state
keep CPU cumulative references per phase
write reports/persistent_resident_state_abi_probe_summary.json only after compare reports exist for every phase
prove phase > 1 init-state reload remains rejected
prove measured summary cannot be written without all phase compares

implemented_storage.device_storage_authority: the same d_storage allocation advances all four phases
implemented_storage.next_phase_input: existing device d_storage contents, not previous phase dump file

non_claims: not paged attention or KV-cache scale-up
